findings.text: §7 adds `claim_sources_for_candidates`, `release_candidate_claim`, `has_pending_candidate_work and candidate_worker` "beside their mapping counterparts", a third near-copy of the claim machinery that is already duplicated once: `claim_sources_for_assignment` (workers.py:136) and `claim_sources_for_mapping` (workers.py:199) are the same claim-token + `ORDER BY rand()` + cutoff query differing only in the status predicate and returned properties, and the release/`has_pending` helpers (`workers.py:274,287,303,329,343`) repeat the same shape; the plan multiplies the surface again rather than extending the owner with a claim routine parameterized by (from-status, claim property names, returned fields); the census of the duplicated family is workers.py:136, 199, 274, 287, 303, 329, 343.

findings.reason: the honest change is to move the existing shortlist construction out of `mapping.py` into `candidates.py` and re-point retrieval at `hybrid_dd_search`, so the cluster-expansion/dedup code is not written twice and §8's retirement becomes a deletion rather than a rewrite.
findings.text: §4 creates a new module `imas_codex/ids/candidates.py` whose job — build a per-source shortlist of embedded DD nodes, expand it through semantic clusters, dedup — is already performed by `gather_shared_context`, which constructs `source_candidates` at `mapping.py:781–854` (vector hits at 782–794, cluster expansion via `cluster_searcher.search_by_path` at 803, dedup at 800–801), with the `ClusterSearcher` load at `mapping.py:631–635`; §4 says the legacy "is retired by §8, not by this section", so the plan knowingly writes fresh orchestration rather than lifting the existing construction (its cluster-expansion and dedup logic) into the new owner.

findings.reason: with all four supplied counts at 0, each section that moves a counter off zero must account for the added surface in its own text; §5 in particular should name what it retires (or say why it cannot) rather than adding a parallel judgment module and seat unaccounted.
